body:
meredith@shadow.net (William R. Meredith) wrote:
:
: Technology save lives AND does not place anyone at greater risk of death.
: There are many ways of dying now as in the past but we are running less
: and less risk of dying young now then at any other time in history thank
: to technology.

You have laid the groundwork for an interesting discussion:  What is
more important - the number of lives or the quality of them?

Certainly with technology we could eventually remove nearly all risk
and variation from lives and keep billions of people alive.  But
what about being able to be free and do something meaningful other
than serve the system and be controlled by the system?

: : Entirely untrue. It's not the lifestyle that he was objecting to, it's the
: : entire foundation of society to which these people were contributing.
:
: Same thing IE they was living a life style that was contributing to things
: he did not agree with so he kill them and he did take it upon himself the
: right to kill anyone who did anything he did not agree with and he was
: very very careless or uncaring about who he harm IE airliners and bombs in
: public places

You're still using a black and white mode of analysis and missing the
fine details.  That's what is keeping us from communicating about the
problems of this world.

: You really think that having someone walking around free who could try to
: kill a few hundred people is a good idea?

And how many lives has technology taken?  And how many millions has it
devalued, making people into slaves to serve the system, stripping
them of hope and suffocating them with regulations and restrictions
on their harmless behavior?

: Hmm the only problem with the idea of giving anyone the power to decide
: that killing a few is ok to save many is that crazy gentleman like Ted and
: you perhaps would use it to justify bombing airliners etc. No I don't wish
: anyone ot have a license to kill be it 007 or Ted.

What about your government?

Is it ok to kill animals?

Is it ok to kill unborn babies?

If yes to the above, then why not individual moral agents?

: My automobiles are evil, well who in the hell is forcing you or your
: girlfriend to use them??????????????

Society requires many people to use cars just to keep up.

: You wish to live in a culture without cars?????????

   129. Another reason why technology is such a powerful social force is
   that, within the context of a given society, technological progress
   marches in only one direction; it can never be reversed. Once a
   technical innovation has been introduced, people usually become
   dependent on it, unless it is replaced by some still more advanced
   innovation. Not only do people become dependent as individuals on a
   new item of technology, but, even more, the system as a whole becomes
   dependent on it. (Imagine what would happen to the system today if
   computers, for example, were eliminated.) Thus the system can move in
   only one direction, toward greater technologization. Technology
   repeatedly forces freedom to take a step back -- short of the
   overthrow of the whole technological system.

: You know you can do so without the need of killing anyone? Amish don't use
: cars and they are a peaceful people. Go live with them.

I'm not sure the Amish accept outsiders into their culture, but even
the Amish are probably not happy about the intrusions that technology
introduced into their lives (noise from airplanes and cars, pollution
from factories, etc).

You're avoiding what the original poster was expressing.  Once 
technology becomes widespread, everyone has to keep up or be left
behind.  If you don't have a car now, you are considered primitive.
Soon everyone will need an Internet account.  Then we'll all need
a full-time cellular hook up on our personal communication agents.
Already in the tech world many people have cell phones and pagers
so they can receive human and computer communication at any time.
I happen to think communication is probably good, but these people
are communicating (or rather being communicated at) for the sake
of maintaining the system.

:: At what cost? Does it make you sad that animals in the wild die of
:: diseases? 
:
: My a course on logic 101 would be very helpful to you!!!!!!!!!!!!
:
: Statemnt my girlfriend could die because of evil technology.
:
: Answer, but she is more likely to live longer now then in the past.

Not true.  She is only less likely to die in child birth or the
early years.  Also technology promises that her life will be less
free and more controlled.  She is more likely to have to serve the
system and be forced to neglect her own needs.

: Statement but so what she is not happy!  I am sorry she is not happy but
: who would be with you in their life?

Because the system dominates her life and prevents her individuality
from being developed and her needs from being pursued, while suffocating
her with restrictions and limitations.

: Hell you support Ted right to kill others do you not and his bombings do
: you not? So I guess you wish Ted to have a license to kill but not
: yourself? Why not, as like your hero you can see how bombings and killings
: are usefull. Why don't you go after all those evil men that are mading
: your life hell?  

It is possible to see acts of revolution, such as bombings, to be useful
without wanting to kill others.  

It is not possible to "go after those evil men that are [making] your 
life hell" because they are the agents of the system and they control
the system.  They're the ones making laws that restrict your freedom,
they're the ones marketing plastic toys for you to buy, they're the
ones selling you junk food, they're the ones producing entertainment
so you don't focus on the problems of this world.  And they have the
power to set values in this society, so they are above being held
responsible for their actions since whatever they do is defined as 
"good".

:: Which others? Would you advocate the death penalty for TK if convicted?
:: Where's your compassion now?
:
: I find it very hard to feel compassion to a sociopath that randomly try to
: kill his fellow humans and as I do support the right of self defense and
: the right to punish a murderer, I would cheerfully carry out the
: sentence of a court myself and then have a good night sleep. 

What about the devaluation of human life which has occured because
of the system?  Isn't that more painful than death because it must
be endured by millions of people?

: As far as I know, unlike Ted you have not broken the social contract and
: kill anyone and I hope you do not.

What social contract?  I never signed any such thing.  There's no 
evidence that such a thing exists.  The government kills people all
of the time and you're even in favor of killing Dr. Kaczynski.

: I don't have the right to kill people I disagree with, you don't have the
: right to kill people you disagree with and Ted don't have a license to
: kill.

Sure.  But it's not able disagreements.  It's about impositions on 
the freedoms of others.  This line of discussion will make a lot
more sense 50-100 years from now if things continue in the direction
they are going now.  Technology could be useful to everyone and
could improve our lifestyle and increase or freedom, but it continues
to be abused and could ultimately restrict human freedom almost entirely.

-Ric
